gaps.sentence: The mixture will ___ as it cools (SOLID).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: solidify means to become solid. A base verb follows 'will'.

gaps.sentence: Her kindness and ___ (GENEROUS) made her very popular.
gaps.explanation: Parallel to 'kindness', a noun is needed: generosity (note the irregular -osity spelling).

gaps.sentence: Do you believe in the ___ (EXIST) of life on other planets?
gaps.explanation: After 'the' a noun is needed: existence (-ence noun).

gaps.sentence: There are many ___ (SIMILAR) between the two languages.
gaps.explanation: 'Many' needs a plural countable noun: similarities (note the -ty to -ties spelling).

gaps.hint: person needed (-ist for fields of study)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ist forms the person who studies a subject: biology becomes biologist.

gaps.sentence: I'm afraid your passport is ___ — it expired last month (VALID).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: it has expired
gaps.explanation: An expired document is invalid (in- + valid); an adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ to accept the conditions at first (WILLING).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: she did not want to
gaps.explanation: 'At first' suggests reluctance, so the negative adjective 'unwilling' (un- + willing) is needed.

gaps.sentence: The campaign aims to raise ___ of road safety (AWARE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ness forms the noun: raise awareness is the fixed phrase; 'aware' is an adjective.
